FIG. 12 is flow chart illustrating the process of setting marking bit associated with referenced field within an object in accordance with an embodiment of the   present invention: First, the system receives a reference to the field within the object (step 1202) This reference may be read Or a write operation. (Note that in the case of an array object the field is an array element.)

In one embodiment of the present invention, the marking bit   is identified by performing modulo   operation. For example, if the object includes N marking bits numbered 0, 1, 2, N-1 and M fields numbered 0, 1, 2, M-1, the   system starts:with field   number for the   field, and a modulo N operation to the field number to produce number   for the associated marking   bit. This modulo operation can be efficiently performed if Nis a power of two because the modulo operation reduces to simple bit mask operation that   isolates the lower order bits of the field number. applies The selection value of N for an object   involves tradeoff. If Nis too small, there tends to be lot of aliasing and 10   system performance suffers due to false rollbacks. If N is too large, great deal of memory is used for marking bits which can cause cache performance to suffer. In one embodiment of the present   invention; N=8 In another   embodiment, N=16

The   above-described  mapping between array elements and marking bits for array objects associates consecutive array locations with single marking bit. This ensures that not all of the marking bits are set by common block copy operations involving only portion of the array.

In   general the marking mechanism   according to the present invention can be used in any application that must track of accesses to fields within an object. However, in one   embodiment  of the present  invention; marking is performed for read operations by speculative thread 203. After the marking bits have been set, if a head thread 202 subsequently performs a  write operation to field in the object, head thread 202 can identify the associated marking bit using the above-described modulo or division operations.
